title: Who is who on the voyage
back: Tishani Doshi (traveller-writer), Geoff Green (Students on Ice), the high-school students (future policy-makers).

title: The journey in six beats
back: Madras → Gondwana → 12,000 years → Students on Ice → phytoplankton → walk on the ocean.

title: Gondwana
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="The supercontinent in Antarctica's rocks and ice" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><circle cx="160" cy="95" r="70" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.15" stroke="none"/><path d="M110,80 Q140,50 180,70 Q210,100 190,130 Q150,140 120,120 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><text x="160" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="700" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">650 million years ago</text><text x="160" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">India and Antarctica, one landmass</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">The supercontinent in Antarctica's rocks and ice</text></svg>
back: Warm and human-free; it broke apart after the dinosaurs. Ice-cores hold half a million years of carbon records.

title: A blanket of carbon dioxide
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="What humans did in a few seconds of Earth's time" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><circle cx="160" cy="110" r="60" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><circle cx="160" cy="110" r="80" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="10"/><text x="160" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">12,000 years</text><text x="160" y="185" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">a blink on the geological clock</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">What humans did in a few seconds of Earth's time</text></svg>
back: Cities, wars, population, fossil fuels; the temperature rises. Will the West Antarctic ice sheet melt? Will the Gulf Stream be disrupted?

title: Students on Ice
back: Celebrities could give nothing back; students absorb, learn and act. Seeing a glacier retreat changes a person as no textbook can.
